I've been working this land since I was 18, and I know Quzhou's soils and seasons as well as I know my own hands. My 9 mu breaks down simply: 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation that anchors everything, and 3 mu of cotton on the side plot. My husband and I can handle this without hiring labor if I plan it right.

**Wheat (6 mu, winter):** I'll plant Jimai 22 — I've used it for years and it performs reliably in our alkaline soils. I rotary-till after maize harvest in October, apply compound fertilizer as base, then urea at jointing. Three irrigations: one at sowing to ensure germination, one before winter dormancy, one at jointing. Aphids and rust are predictable problems here, so three pesticide applications — a herbicide early on, then two more through heading. I expect around 450 kg/mu.

**Maize (6 mu, summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed Xianyu 335 hybrid — no plowing, straight into stubble. Time is tight during the wheat-maize handoff. I push nitrogen hard at the V6-V8 stage. Summer rainfall helps, but I'll irrigate twice — once at silking if it's dry, once at grain fill. Two pesticide passes for armyworm and aphids. Targeting 600 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3 mu, spring/summer):** Cotton is getting harder at my age — the picking especially. But the market was decent last year and I know this crop. I'll plow this plot in spring, plant hybrid seed. Cotton needs real attention: I'll irrigate four times and stay on top of bollworm and spider mites with seven pesticide applications spread through the season. I expect 250 kg/mu of seed cotton.
